slots.label: need-based individual change
slots.description: Individual birds grow deeper beaks during their lives because they need them.
slots.repair: Selection changes populations across generations by sorting existing heritable variation, not by need-driven change in individuals.
slots.repairQuestion: In the drought example, what changes during an individual bird's life and what changes across generations?
slots.repairCriteria: Repaired when the learner says individuals do not evolve their beaks from need; populations change over generations.

slots.label: survival-only fitness
slots.description: Natural selection is only about which individuals survive, not whether they reproduce.
slots.repair: Survival matters because it can affect reproductive contribution, but evolutionary fitness is about leaving offspring or genes in the next generation.
slots.repairQuestion: Why is reproduction essential in natural selection?
slots.repairCriteria: Repaired when the learner connects fitness to offspring or contribution to the next generation.

slots.label: progress misconception
slots.description: Natural selection always makes organisms more advanced, perfect, or complex.
slots.repair: Selection favors traits in a particular environment; it has no general direction toward perfection or complexity.
slots.repairQuestion: Why might a trait be favored in one environment but not another?
slots.repairCriteria: Repaired when the learner says selection is environment-specific and not goal-directed progress.

slots.text: Natural selection requires existing heritable variation, environmental differences in survival or reproduction, and resulting changes in trait or allele frequencies across generations. It acts through individuals' reproductive success but evolution is a population-level outcome. It is not need-based, intentional, or goal-directed.
